candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Genesis
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Genesis, Section XII. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13, ed. J. Gwynn / Schaff (1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Genesis (c. 360 AD)

Ephrem reads the call of Abram as the prototype of every later monastic-renunciation: 'Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto a land that I will shew thee'. The threefold renunciation (country/kindred/father's house) anticipates the Lord's later threefold demand in Lk 14:26-33. Ephrem notes that Abram is asked to leave a land of moon-worship (Ur of the Chaldees was a centre of the Sin/lunar cult) precisely because he is to become the father of those who worship the Lord of heaven — the geographical exit IS a theological exit. Tewahedo monastic tradition preserves Ephrem's reading: every monk's withdrawal repeats Abram's.

candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Genesis (c. 360 AD)

First theophany: 'And the Lord appeared unto Abram'. Ephrem emphasises that the Word who appears here is the same Word who became flesh — the Father is invisible, but the Word makes Himself visible through theophanies. The altar Abram builds is the FIRST altar of true worship in the land that will become the holy land, prefiguring every later altar in the Mosaic-Aaronic priesthood and ultimately the Tewahedo tabot. Tewahedo eucharistic theology preserves Ephrem's identification of the OT theophanies as appearances of the pre-incarnate Word.
